instruction: Download the image from the given link, rotate it clockwise by 90 degrees with GIMP, and store the result as 'rotated.jpeg' on your Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "alt", "t"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires rotating the downloaded image 90 degrees clockwise using GIMP. The original kingbird.jpeg is landscape (wider than tall), so after 90-degree clockwise rotation it becomes portrait (taller than wide). Custom getter extracts dimensions and determines if image is portrait orientation (height > width), custom metric verifies is_portrait is true. Similar complexity to original (download, open GIMP, perform operation, save file).

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Evaluator checks all three critical aspects - portrait orientation, dimension swapping, and content preservation
Dimension swap verification (gimp.py:87-88): Correctly checks rotated.width == original.height AND rotated.height == original.width, which verifies the 90-degree rotation was applied

Content preservation verification (gimp.py:79-92): Getter rotates original image 90° clockwise (-90 in PIL) and compares perceptual hashes with tolerance of 5, which correctly verifies the rotation was performed on the correct image with correct direction
Robust logic: Getter handles edge case where original image is not found (gimp.py:104-107), setting verification flags to False

Semantically correct: The three-part verification (is_portrait + dimensions_swapped + content_preserved) together ensure the task was completed correctly - rotation direction, rotation application, and content identity are all verified
